chains.title: TFAP2A binds the ref A allele more strongly; the risk G allele weakens the IRF6 enhancer and lowers IRF6
chains.cell_type: developing oral epithelium/periderm at the lip

links.claim: TFAP2A binds the ref A allele more strongly than the alt G allele at rs642961; the G allele is predicted to disrupt an AP-2-binding site. TFAP2A was chosen as the AP-2-family member most consistent with the known IRF6 enhancer biology; QBiC-SELEX coverage is not_checked because no screen or qbic_tf_detail evidence was supplied.
rs642961 lies in the IRF6 MCS9.7 enhancer; the A allele preserves an enhancer sequence that can be bound by TFAP2A, while the G allele weakens it.
The TFAP2A-bound IRF6 enhancer element promotes IRF6 transcription.
The relevant cell type is developing oral epithelium/periderm at the lip, with possible contributions from cranial neural crest-derived lip mesenchyme.
Reduced IRF6 dosage in the developing lip impairs epithelial fusion and increases cleft lip risk.

predictions: TFAP2A binds the A allele more than the G allele at rs642961.
The A allele preserves higher enhancer activity than the G allele in an IRF6 enhancer reporter.
IRF6 expression is lower when the G allele is present in the relevant craniofacial epithelial context.
The phenotype is consistent with reduced IRF6 dosage increasing cleft lip risk.
falsified_if: TFAP2A shows no reproducible allele-specific binding to rs642961 probes.
The G allele does not reduce IRF6 enhancer activity or IRF6 expression in the relevant cell context.

chains.title: No TF-mediated allelic effect at rs642961; association is due to a linked causal variant or passenger signal
predictions: rs642961 itself does not alter TF binding or enhancer activity.
Any association with cleft lip is explained by linkage disequilibrium with another variant.
Allele-specific TFAP2A binding is not reproducible.
falsified_if: rs642961 shows reproducible allele-specific TF binding and enhancer activity in the relevant cell context.

chains.title: Opposite-direction TFAP2A chain: the alt G allele binds TFAP2A more strongly and represses IRF6
chains.cell_type: developing oral epithelium/periderm at the lip

links.claim: TFAP2A binds the alt G allele more strongly than the ref A allele at rs642961. QBiC-SELEX coverage is not_checked because no screen or qbic_tf_detail evidence was supplied.
The G allele creates or strengthens a TFAP2A-responsive sequence in the IRF6 MCS9.7 enhancer.
Increased TFAP2A occupancy at this element represses IRF6 transcription.
The relevant cell type is developing oral epithelium/periderm at the lip.
Reduced IRF6 expression increases cleft lip risk.

predictions: TFAP2A binds the G allele more than the A allele at rs642961.
The G allele increases TFAP2A occupancy and reduces IRF6 enhancer activity if TFAP2A acts as a repressor in this context.
IRF6 expression is lower with the G allele, but through increased rather than decreased TFAP2A binding.
falsified_if: TFAP2A binds the A allele more strongly than the G allele.
The G allele increases rather than decreases IRF6 enhancer activity.

chains.title: TP63 rather than TFAP2A mediates the allelic effect at rs642961
chains.cell_type: developing oral epithelium/periderm at the lip

links.claim: TP63 binds the ref A allele more strongly than the alt G allele at rs642961. TP63 QBiC-SELEX coverage is not_checked because no screen or qbic_tf_detail evidence was supplied.
rs642961 lies within an IRF6 enhancer that can be regulated by TP63-responsive sequences.
TP63-bound enhancer activity contributes to IRF6 transcription.
The relevant cell type is developing oral epithelium/periderm at the lip.
Reduced TP63-dependent IRF6 expression increases cleft lip risk.

predictions: TP63 binds the ref A allele more than the alt G allele at rs642961.
The G allele reduces TP63-dependent IRF6 enhancer activity.
TFAP2A allelic binding is not the primary driver.
falsified_if: TP63 shows no allele-specific binding to rs642961.
TFAP2A, not TP63, accounts for the allele-specific enhancer effect.

matrix.test: TFAP2A binding to ref vs alt probe

outcomes.outcome: Much stronger binding to ref A than alt G

next_experiment: Allele-specific EMSA with recombinant TFAP2A and short dsDNA probes centered on rs642961 (ref A vs alt G), with cold competitor and, if available, TFAP2A antibody supershift. A reproducible ref>alt binding difference supports the TFAP2A-loss chain; no allele-specific binding supports the null.
